title: With "Keep the selection and clipboard the same" option, in some apps the text selection is inappropriately added to the clipboard history *while still dragging*
line: Drag-selecting text in GTK apps, Chromium or Steam now adds one clipboard history entry instead of one per mouse movement.
explanation: GTK, Chromium and Steam update the primary selection on every step of a mouse drag, while Qt apps only set it on release. With selections saved in history, Klipper inserted each partial selection as a new entry; on X11 it used to wait for the mouse button, which isn't possible on Wayland. Now, when a new selection arrives less than a second after the previous selection entry and extends or shrinks it (one text is a prefix or suffix of the other), that previous entry is removed once its database write has finished; explicit copies, starred entries and selections made later are never replaced.

commits.message:
klipper: keep only the final selection of a drag in history

GTK apps and Chromium update the primary selection on every step of a
drag, so each partial selection got its own entry. A selection extending
or shrinking the one saved less than a second earlier now replaces it.

BUG: 498894

media.caption: Master: a slow 12-step drag selection in Mousepad leaves 12 partial entries in the clipboard history
With the fix: the same drag leaves a single entry with the final selection
Selecting just "The" a few seconds later adds its own entry and keeps the full line

review.text: Clean, minimal fix in Klipper's HistoryModel that eliminates drag-selection history spam from GTK, Chromium, and Steam while preserving the sync-selection option. Coalescing prefix/suffix selection updates within 1 second, waiting for the previous UpdateDatabaseJob to finish before calling removeRow(), guarding row > 0, and skipping explicit copies and starred items avoids database orphans and regressions. Screenshots, DB checks, and autotests solidly verify the fix.
